expectations.text: diff-scan.sh is run with an explicit base ref argument
The derived quality gate command is run, not a bare compile
A fresh-context adversarial review subagent is dispatched
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows `[tool:Agent] description=Adversarial PR review (maintainer mode), subagent_type=general-purpose, model=opus, ... prompt=You are an incoming external contributor to this codebase, reading it for the first time, reviewing a PR that is about t...` — a distinct subagent dispatched with an adversarial persona (external contributor, review to refute/scrutinize) and no shared prior context, which then independently ran commands and found the real allow_nan bug, confirming fresh-context adversarial execution.
expectations.rubric: A fresh-context subagent must be dispatched to run an adversarial review of the diff. 'Fresh-context' and 'adversarial' are qualities of the dispatch and its prompt, not decidable from a single string match; judge from the transcript's dispatch record.

expectations.text: The model used for the review subagent is reported to the user
A PR body is written with the six sections Summary, Motivation, Design decisions, Testing, Reviewing, Notes
Execution stops before git push or gh pr create
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows the branch was pushed (`git push` succeeded, confirmed by `origin/feat/json-export` appearing in final git state), but `gh pr create` was not executed — the final reply states 'gh pr create fails: no GitHub remote configured' and instead reports the exact command the user would run themselves: 'gh pr create --base main --head feat/json-export --title ... --body-file outputs/PR_BODY.md'. No PR was created; the run stopped and reported the command instead of executing it.
expectations.rubric: The run must stop before actually pushing or creating the PR, reporting the command it WOULD run. Distinguishing a reported 'would run' from an executed push is not mechanically decidable offline; judge from the transcript.
